flagged.evidence: The proof says the crossed-product identity transports crossings “with the same direction sign.” Relative to the fixed D in the Statement, this can fail: for the A1 root datum X=Zα, Y=Zω∨ with ⟨α,ω∨⟩=1, take A=(0,1) and Ω generated by ω(x)=1−x. Ω swaps the wall reflections s0 at x=1 and s1 at x=0. With D pointing toward +∞, A→s0A=(1,2) is positive, while its Ω-image A→s1A=(−1,0) is negative. The sign is preserved only if D is transported too. Restricting the argument to the stated canonical affine-word-plus-Ω form avoids this extra inference, so the main statement is unaffected.
